page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a high-capacity server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The configuration provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 48 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is a key feature, consisting of 23038 GB of NVMe SSD storage, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included, and there are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier multi-core performance and exceptional memory bandwidth. The multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests both rank in the top 10%, supported by a top-tier PassMark CPU score and PassMark CPU encryption test. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block cached read-only bandwidth reaching the top 10% (7287.47 GB/sec), while large-block uncached read and write operations rank in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing also achieve top-tier status. However, single-threaded performance is slightly more moderate; single-core stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores rank in the top 25%, while single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression fall into the middle 50%. Database operations are highly performant, with Redis SET operations reaching the top 10% at 122.77 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations ranking in the top 25%. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference prompt processing for small and medium models ranks in the top 10% and top 25% respectively, though text generation speeds for large models remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L96as_v4 offers high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage with a substantial memory-to-vCPU ratio. This makes it highly qualitative for data-intensive workloads that require rapid local read/write access without the overhead of external storage arrays. The primary tradeoff is the lack of GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it remains capable of CPU-based LLM inference. The instance is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput data warehousing, big data analytics, software compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a high-capacity, storage-optimized server from the Lasv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores), 768.0 GB of RAM, and a massive 23038 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating at 3.7 GHz, the x86_64 CPU supports AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerations. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core performance, exceptional cached memory bandwidth, and outstanding database throughput, with Redis SET operations reaching the top 10%. While single-core performance and large-model text generation are more moderate, the instance excels in multi-threaded tasks, software compilation, and data processing. Lacking a GPU, it trades specialized acceleration for dense local storage and high memory capacity. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale databases, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
